text:
Ryan Strome is 33, on his fifth NHL team, and in his first full season with Calgary he is doing what he's always done: move the puck and keep a line afloat. Thirteen points in 26 games is a league-average scoring rate in 14.6 minutes a night, and CBS Sports had him at six points in six games heading into last week.

The Flames are better with him on. They take 53.1% of the 5v5 shot attempts and get 3.6 more points of expected goal share than without him. His own finishing lags: 9.8% of his shots go in against a 13.5% league rate, though 5 goals on 4.7 expected says his looks are modest rather than wasted.

That fits Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season. He shoots a lot (10.2 attempts per 60, 81st percentile) but fewer come from the slot than the volume suggests, and he carries the puck in on only 31% of his entries. The thing to watch is whether he gets inside. When he does, as against Chicago's Spencer Knight on Nov. 21, the goals follow.
headline: Strome is producing; the shots aren't going in
